tiles.visual_brief: Guangzhou CTF has a pale, vertically ribbed facade, asymmetric setbacks and a split-height crown. It stands beside K11 and Guangzhou Library; Huacheng Square and Pearl River viewpoints reveal its recognizable profile. Distinguish it from the rounded Guangzhou IFC West Tower, lattice-waisted Canton Tower and smoothly tapered Tianjin CTF.
tiles.notes: Six distinct photographs retained; c1 recommended. All passed JPEG decoding, dimension checks and visual inspection. No visible watermarks. Source pages state no reuse licence. References were not reused. Node handled downloads after Python was unavailable and curl failed TLS.

tiles.visual_brief: Tianjin CTF is a blue-silver glass tower with a broad base, softly tapering sides and a rounded, multi-lobed crown. Sweeping curved ribs distinguish its facade above the relatively low TEDA/Binhai district; nearby streets and landscaped plazas offer recognizable full-height views. Avoid confusing it with boxy Goldin Finance 117, stepped Guangzhou CTF or pointed Lotte World Tower.
tiles.notes: Seven distinct photographs retained; c1 and c2 recommended. All passed JPEG decoding, dimensions and visual inspection, with no visible watermarks. c1-c4 are larger SOM originals; c5-c7 have 1799-pixel long sides. Source pages credit Seth Powers but state no reuse licence. Repository follow-up check could not run because Python was unavailable. Writes stayed within the requested folders.
